sites.rationale: The ledger explicitly names P194 and G195 as the junction residues for pHluorin insertion in full-length membrane-anchored human DAT. Python lookup confirms sequence[194]='P' and sequence[195]='G'. Both positions fall within EL2 (165–235), 30 residues from TM3 end (164) and 41 residues from TM4 start (236), well clear of the ≥3-residue TM boundary constraint. Multiple independent studies (pHluorin, HA, HA-βlac) converge on this exact junction, and surface display plus trafficking function were directly measured. pHluorin inserted between P194 and G195 in the second extracellular loop (EL2) of full-length human DAT; construct selected for further validation after initial screen of five EL2 sites. Surface display confirmed by non-permeabilized cell staining; cocaine-induced internalization tracked in real time. Prior HA epitope insertion at the same junction (referenced as refs 49,50 in PMC9804146) and HA-βlactamase insertion at the same site (PMC9124866) used in a microplate surface-expression assay for pharmacological chaperone screening. Tetracysteine CCPGCC also placed at the intrinsic PG194-195 motif (PMC2817725), though that modification reduced DA uptake. [validation: surface_and_function; position: inferred; source: paper; cited_tag_residue: 194; entailment_verified: True]

sites.rationale: The ledger reports a tetracysteine modification in EL3 of full-length DAT. The paper does not give an exact insertion junction, only 'EL3'. Python analysis identifies the intrinsic PG motif at positions 288-289 within EL3 (286-309) as the likely target (the paper states they used intrinsic PG motifs). Position 288 is 3 residues from TM5 end (285) and 21 residues from TM6 start (310). This is a region-level site; insert_after_residue is null. Ranked low due to function_perturbed status and region-level (not residue-level) evidence. Tetracysteine CCPGCC sequence engineered into EL3 of full-length DAT (DAT EL3-CCPGCC) by mutating the 2 upstream and downstream residues flanking the intrinsic PG motif (PG at 288-289 in EL3, 286-309). Construct expressed and used in FlAsH/ReAsH labeling experiments. However, significantly reduced DA uptake was observed compared to wildtype DAT (p<0.01), indicating functional perturbation. [validation: function_perturbed; position: inferred; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

literature_notes: Seven sites reported, all extracellular, all grounded in the ledger. EXCLUDED: (1) C-terminal Twin-Strep-HA and FLAG tags (PMC7809260) — the C-terminus of DAT (residues 579-620) is intracellular per the topology landmarks; these tags are not extracellular. (2) YFP N-terminal fusion in YFP-HA-DAT (PMC8010718) — the N-terminus (residues 1-68) is intracellular; the YFP tag is not extracellular. The HA in YFP-HA-DAT is in EL2 at the same P194/G195 site already covered by PMC9804146. (3) DAT-pHluorin neuron protocol (PMC11490699) — this is the same P194/G195 construct as PMC9804146, used in neurons; it adds no new site. The G199/S201 site is reported with insert_after_residue=199 because G199 is the named residue before the junction; the actual next residue in the canonical sequence is D200, not S201 as the paper states — this one-residue discrepancy in the paper's notation is flagged in the rationale. The EL3 and EL4 tetracysteine sites are region-level only (no junction residue named in the paper) and both showed significantly reduced DA uptake, making them poor candidates for a functionally silent tag.
